harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Added a 512 MB lzo-compressed zram swap device on node1, configured to start at boot via a systemd oneshot unit (zram-swap.service, enabled for multi-user.target and swap.target) with priority 100 — higher than the existing disk-backed swap (/dev/vda2, priority -2) — so zram is preferred. Verified the setup survives a real node reboot (boot_id changed from 0d6209e2... to b8697ca4...) with zram swap active, enabled, and still at higher priority post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: RHEL 7.9, kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7, existing 2GB disk swap on /dev/vda2 (priority -2), no zram-generator package available (RHEL7's systemd 219 predates it), zram kernel module present supporting lzo compression
Wrote /usr/local/sbin/zram-swap-start and zram-swap-stop scripts: modprobe zram, set comp_algorithm=lzo, set disksize=512M, mkswap /dev/zram0, swapon -p 100 /dev/zram0
Created /etc/systemd/system/zram-swap.service (Type=oneshot, RemainAfterExit=yes) and enabled it for multi-user.target and swap.target so it activates at boot
Started the service and verified zram0 (512MB, lzo) active as swap at priority 100 vs disk swap at -2; re-enabled disk swap alongside it

Captured baseline boot_id (0d6209e2...) and swap state, rebooted node1 via 'sudo shutdown -r now' (acknowledgement returned before disconnect), polled until reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed to b8697ca4..., and re-verified zram swap active/enabled with correct priority after the real restart

evidence.requirement: At least 512MB of compressed in-memory swap added
evidence.summary: zram0 created with disksize 536870912 bytes (512M) and comp_algorithm lzo, then added as active swap via mkswap+swapon

evidence.requirement: zram swap preferred over disk-backed swap
evidence.summary: /proc/swaps shows /dev/zram0 at priority 100 vs /dev/vda2 (disk) at priority -2, both before and after the reboot

evidence.requirement: Active at boot / persistent across restart
evidence.summary: zram-swap.service enabled for multi-user.target and swap.target; baseline boot_id 0d6209e2... captured pre-reboot; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id b8697ca4... confirms a real restart occurred; zram swap shown active/enabled with correct 512MB size and priority 100 after that restart, proving the systemd unit brought it back automatically
